scene_0_morning_brief.speaker: Rose
scene_0_morning_brief.text: Old slippers, balikbayan. Ones you don't love.

scene_0_morning_brief.speaker: Papa Jobert
scene_0_morning_brief.text: \Bakhawan? I used to fish there. Off the mud, before there were any trees.

scene_0_morning_brief.speaker: Lola Jonabel
scene_0_morning_brief.text: Every Saturday. You came home smelling like the sea.

scene_0_morning_brief.speaker: Rose
scene_0_morning_brief.text: Then you're coming, Tito. Someone has to pull the balikbayan out when they sink.

scene_0_morning_brief.speaker: Lola Susan
scene_0_morning_brief.text: Manong Ambo knows the tides. Listen to him.

scene_0_morning_brief.speaker: Lola Jonabel
scene_0_morning_brief.text: I'll stay. My knees and boardwalks don't get along. Bring me a story.

scene_1_arrival_at_the_eco_park.speaker: Rose
scene_1_arrival_at_the_eco_park.translation: This is the mangrove. It's not just for visitors, it's for protection.

scene_1_arrival_at_the_eco_park.speaker: Player
scene_1_arrival_at_the_eco_park.text: It looks peaceful. I didn't expect it to be this wide.

scene_1_arrival_at_the_eco_park.speaker: Manong Ambo
scene_1_arrival_at_the_eco_park.translation: [GoodDay], visitors. Are you here to see our mangroves?

scene_1_arrival_at_the_eco_park.speaker: Rose
scene_1_arrival_at_the_eco_park.text: \Huo means yes, balikbayan. He's the caretaker here. Say hello properly.

choices.label: Can we skip to the fishing?

scene_1_arrival_at_the_eco_park.speaker: Manong Ambo
scene_1_arrival_at_the_eco_park.translation: Come here, apo. Let's get going.

scene_1_arrival_at_the_eco_park.speaker: Rose
scene_1_arrival_at_the_eco_park.text: Manners, balikbayan. The fish aren't going anywhere.

scene_2_learning_about_mangroves.speaker: Manong Ambo
scene_2_learning_about_mangroves.translation: Because the roots hold on to the soil, it won't be destroyed even by a storm.

scene_2_learning_about_mangroves.speaker: Rose
scene_2_learning_about_mangroves.text: That's why they say mangroves are natural shields.

scene_2_learning_about_mangroves.speaker: Papa Jobert
scene_2_learning_about_mangroves.text: When I was a boy, there was nothing here. Just mud. The sea came right up to the houses when it stormed.

scene_2_learning_about_mangroves.speaker: Manong Ambo
scene_2_learning_about_mangroves.translation: In 1990, this was all just mud. We planted them one by one.

scene_2_learning_about_mangroves.speaker: Manong Ambo
scene_2_learning_about_mangroves.translation: Me and the people who wanted to help.

scene_2_learning_about_mangroves.speaker: Rose
scene_2_learning_about_mangroves.text: \Ugat. Roots. The thing holding you up, balikbayan.

scene_3_fishing_lesson.speaker: Manong Ambo
scene_3_fishing_lesson.translation: Do you want to try fishing? Not just for the fish, but for learning.

choices.label: Yes, I want to learn how.
Maybe later, I just want to watch first.
I'm not really into fishing, sorry.

scene_3_fishing_lesson.speaker: Manong Ambo
scene_3_fishing_lesson.translation: There we go! Here, follow me.

scene_3_fishing_lesson.speaker: Papa Jobert
scene_3_fishing_lesson.text: Come on. One try. My father showed me right about here.

scene_3_fishing_lesson.speaker: Rose
scene_3_fishing_lesson.text: You'll miss out. It's part of the experience, balikbayan.

scene_3_fishing_lesson.speaker: Rose
scene_3_fishing_lesson.text: And I'm not touching the bait, so it's you or nobody.

scene_3_fishing_lesson.speaker: Manong Ambo
scene_3_fishing_lesson.translation: The hook, and the bait. Be careful with it.

scene_3_fishing_lesson.speaker: Rose
scene_3_fishing_lesson.text: He means don't yank it like you did the loom.

scene_3_fishing_lesson.speaker: Papa Jobert
scene_3_fishing_lesson.text: Beginner's luck. Runs in the family.

scene_3_fishing_lesson.speaker: Manong Ambo
scene_3_fishing_lesson.translation: It's still small. Let's put it back in the water.

scene_3_fishing_lesson.speaker: Rose
scene_3_fishing_lesson.text: The fish won. Don't take it personally.

scene_3_fishing_lesson.speaker: Manong Ambo
scene_3_fishing_lesson.translation: No problem, apo. Just keep at it.

scene_4_vocabulary_practice_round_nature.speaker: Rose
scene_4_vocabulary_practice_round_nature.text: \Tikang \pa, keep walking. \Pamati, listen. \Pamunit, to fish. \Tanom, plant.

scene_4_vocabulary_practice_round_nature.speaker: Player
scene_4_vocabulary_practice_round_nature.text: Okay, so \pamunit is what Manong Ambo said earlier.

scene_4_vocabulary_practice_round_nature.speaker: Rose
scene_4_vocabulary_practice_round_nature.text: Correct. And \tanom, you'll hear that a lot here, since mangroves are plants.

scene_4_vocabulary_practice_round_nature.speaker: Rose
scene_4_vocabulary_practice_round_nature.text: Not bad. You're only a little bit \maeuya.

scene_4_vocabulary_practice_round_nature.speaker: Rose
scene_4_vocabulary_practice_round_nature.text: We'll do it again on the walk home. And again.

scene_4c_after_planting.speaker: Manong Ambo
scene_4c_after_planting.translation: Before long, it'll be taller than you.

scene_4c_after_planting.speaker: Player
scene_4c_after_planting.text: Will it still be here when I come back?

scene_4c_after_planting.speaker: Manong Ambo
scene_4c_after_planting.translation: If someone takes care of it.

scene_4c_after_planting.speaker: Manong Ambo
scene_4c_after_planting.translation: Thanks for visiting, apo. Come back, all of you.

scene_5_reflection.speaker: Papa Jobert
scene_5_reflection.text: This place reminds me of my childhood. Except there were no trees.

scene_5_reflection.speaker: Papa Jobert
scene_5_reflection.text: We left when I was eight. I always thought the shore would look the same when I came back.

scene_5_reflection.speaker: Papa Jobert
scene_5_reflection.text: Someone planted a forest while I was gone. People I never met. And today my kid planted one more.

choices.label: We should come back and check on it.
Can we go? I'm covered in mud.

scene_5_reflection.speaker: Rose
scene_5_reflection.text: And now it's part of yours, balikbayan.

scene_6_evening_home.speaker: Papa Jobert
scene_6_evening_home.translation: We learned so much today. Not just words, but culture too.

scene_6_evening_home.speaker: Lola Jonabel
scene_6_evening_home.text: Listen to him. Fifty years, and now he speaks Akeanon.

scene_6_evening_home.speaker: Papa Jobert
scene_6_evening_home.text: We went to the shore, \Nay. It's a forest now.

scene_6_evening_home.speaker: Lola Jonabel
scene_6_evening_home.text: The mud where you lost your slipper?

scene_6_evening_home.speaker: Lola Susan
scene_6_evening_home.text: Ambo planted those. He and the fishermen, every low tide for years.

scene_6_evening_home.speaker: Lola Jonabel
scene_6_evening_home.text: Then you have a tree in Aklan now, \apo. You'll have to come back and see it.

scene_6_evening_home.speaker: Rose
scene_6_evening_home.text: Wash your feet before you touch anything. Both of you.

examine_kasama_plaque.text: KASAMA: Kalibo Save the Mangroves Association.
Planted 1990 on 50 hectares of mudflat. Today: 220.

examine_trail_sign.text: Boardwalk to the sea. Stay on the bamboo.

examine_watchtower.text: A bamboo watchtower. From the top the forest runs all the way to the sea.

examine_centre_board.text: Bakhawan Eco-Park. Planting began in January 1990 on reclaimed mudflat in New Buswang.
It was planted to stop floods and storm surges. Fishers of KASAMA still look after it.

examine_trail_map.text: Trail map: from the gate the boardwalk winds through the mangroves, past a rest island, out to the sea.

examine_propagules.text: \Bakhawan seedlings, ready to plant. They grow on the tree, then drop into the mud and take root.

examine_guestbook.text: A guestbook. Visitors from all over Aklan, and further, have signed it.

culture_kasama_volunteer.speaker: KASAMA Volunteer
culture_kasama_volunteer.text: Welcome! I'm with KASAMA, the Kalibo Save the Mangroves Association. Most of us are fisherfolk from New Buswang.

culture_kasama_volunteer.speaker: KASAMA Volunteer
culture_kasama_volunteer.text: In 1990 this was bare mudflat. The town planted \bakhawan here so floods and storm surges wouldn't reach the houses.

culture_kasama_volunteer.speaker: KASAMA Volunteer
culture_kasama_volunteer.text: It started with 50 hectares. Now it's about 220, and the bamboo trail runs over a kilometer into the forest.

culture_kasama_volunteer.speaker: KASAMA Volunteer
culture_kasama_volunteer.text: The roots are a nursery too. Young \isda, crabs and shrimp hide there until they're big enough for the sea.

culture_kasama_volunteer.speaker: KASAMA Volunteer
culture_kasama_volunteer.text: Your entrance fee helps us look after it all. Thank you for visiting!
